capabilities: Browse vault files in Yazi's parent/current/preview layout with built-in keybindings
Read the user's keymap.toml and yazi.toml from ~/.config/yazi or pasted settings
Create, rename, move, and trash files through Obsidian so links update
Search by name or content and run shell commands in the current folder
Replace Obsidian's core file explorer in the left sidebar
disambiguation: Not a bridge to the Yazi terminal app; it re-implements Yazi's keymap, layout, and behavior natively inside Obsidian.
extras: Desktop only. Shows the unreviewed-plugin badge in the listing. Yazi config files are optional; some Yazi features (tabs, bulk rename, link/hardlink, task manager, shell --block) are explicitly not supported.
intentEvidence: the same default keys and behavior as Yazi, plus your own keymap.toml and yazi.toml. Nothing new to learn.
problem: Users of the Yazi terminal file manager have to learn a different interaction model for Obsidian's built-in file explorer.

relations.evidence: Key notation, default bindings and behaviour follow Yazi by sxyazi. This plugin is not affiliated with the Yazi project.
When the Iconize plugin is installed, files and folders show the icons and colors assigned there

summary: Vault file explorer that reproduces the Yazi terminal file manager's keys, layout, and config files inside Obsidian.
